name: intelligence-reference-set
status: DRAFT v1 - initial evidence review by an AI agent; reviewed_by_human=false on every record

scoring_rules.negative_population: confirmed_non_material, stale_or_resurfaced, unrelated_incident (duplicate_report is clustered under its parent and not scored for escalation)
scoring_rules.excluded: unresolved_insufficiently_verified is never treated as a negative or a scored positive

measurement_provenance.measured_by_agent: tjr_detection fields (SELECT on intelligence_events/captains_daily_briefs, 2026-11-24, published_at post-repair); export file; scorecard outputs
measurement_provenance.unverified_secondary: all incident facts from standard web search (times, scale, causes) unless an authoritative source is named; see uncertain_facts per record

measured_checks.measured_by: agent, SELECT on production intelligence_events, 2026-11-24, full matching rows (not the sampled export)

incorrect_correlation.PAIR-E: untestable: RS-038 has no TJR events

RS-008.note: (1) Google News copy 'Microsoft access being restored...' stamped 2026-11-12T19:29:40Z, identical to the ABC outage-start item, collected 7 days later: timestamp artefact; (2) iTnews 'Microsoft 365 recovers with Outlook back online' 2026-11-13T03:33Z vs reference end 2026-11-13T16:10Z, but the reference end is itself low-confidence and recovery was progressive: ambiguous

caveats: Web search was standard-mode and US-indexed; many Australian items are thinly sourced.
tjr_detection is title-regex based and indicative.
collected_at is batch time (feed polling and collection lag included).
v0 records are carried over unchanged except status/sector fields and the v1_note/v1_correction annotations.
